answer: An agent economy resists sybils by binding each identity to a scarce domain: a registry accepts an agent only if its key is tied to a CA-validated certificate for a domain whose DNS CAA names the registry as sole issuer and control is proven by a TXT challenge. The registry rejects duplicate domains or keys; a public mirror of certificate logs allows audit. Extra identities cannot wander with the same domain, and a monitoring falcon revokes any second key. Each extra domain costs C per epoch, so n identities gain n(R-C), deterring only while R<C; a rich attacker can still buy domains.
